- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the 30-day horizon, especially after sharp spikes or volatility.
- Model overestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast window, particularly when true outcomes show strong upward momentum or mean reversion.
- Model fails to capture sudden downward corrections after high peaks; it lags behind true price drops by 1–3 days.
- Model exhibits persistent downward bias in low-price regimes (e.g., <35), often undercorrecting or ignoring structural support.
- Model overreacts to recent history, especially when recent prices are high — it tends to overshoot and then correct too slowly.
- Model underestimates the impact of policy or market shocks in the first 5–7 days of the forecast horizon.
- Model shows weak mean reversion behavior — it fails to pull prices back toward historical averages after sharp moves.
- Model is sensitive to the first few days of history — if the last 5–7 days are volatile, it overweights them and misjudges the direction of the next 30 days.
